A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of GSH in the medium is a key factor in the control of the biodegradative pathway of veratrylalcohol.

L. edodes MnP is able to catalyze both the oxidation of the aromatic ring and the side chain oxidation of veratraldehyde to veratric acid, and that GSH is required to obtain the latter pathway, probably by acting as electron donor to the oxidized enzyme.

the presence of a thiol donor in the reaction mixture is a prerequisite for a biodegradative pathway leading to veratraldehyde, while the absence of such a donor is a requirement for a biodegradation pathway leading to aromatic ring fission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of thiol-donors can be used to direct the biodegradative pathway of aromatic compounds, and that the use of L. edodes as biocatalyst can be exploited to this end.
the L. edodes manganese-dependent peroxidases can be used as catalysts for the oxidative dimerization of phenolic compounds.
the presence of a thiol-donating substrate can influence the biodegradative pathway followed by the enzyme, thus affecting the nature of the end-products.
